title: FRT105 coffee (Robusta clone): Characteristics
metaDescription: FRT105 coffee is a robusta coffee variety from Nestle Philippines. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: FRT105 coffee is a robusta coffee variety, also sold or known as Robusta clone or NSIC Cf R 18. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2018 as NSIC 2018 Cf R 18. Nestle Incorporated bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where FRT105 coffee is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Robusta clone or NSIC Cf R 18, this is the same coffee. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [coffee variety finder](/crop-varieties/coffee), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. It first bore fruit about 9 months after planting. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose).

The pests and diseases that hit coffee fields most often: [coffee berry borer](/pests/coffee-berry-borer), [coffee leaf rust](/diseases/coffee-leaf-rust), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** First flowers about 9 months and fruit about 18 months after planting.
**Yield:** About 1.45 kg per tree in Bukidnon, 0.82 kg in Tagum trials.
**Fruit:** Red berries, Grade 1, premium cup score 7.2, medium Robusta body.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: one of Nestle Philippines' registered Robusta clones, graded Grade 1 premium in trials. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant FRT105 coffee

Arabica wants cool highland air, robusta grows in the lowlands, and liberica, the barako, and excelsa are hardy in between. Pick the species for your elevation first, then a selection by yield and cup quality. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Robusta clone the same as FRT105?
items.a: Yes. Robusta clone is another name for FRT105, registered as NSIC 2018 Cf R 18. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of FRT105?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
